text: In this policy, "manager" means the person you report to, "director" means a director or anyone above a director, and "Finance" means the Finance team in the Chicago office.
note: Definitions. Nothing is required of anyone.

text: Spend company money as carefully as you would spend your own.
note: A principle. You cannot test a claim against it.

text: Every claim must be submitted within 30 days of the date the money was spent.
note: Days, not dollars. 30 days is still on time.

text: A receipt must be attached to any claim of $25 or more.
note: $25 or more: exactly $25 needs a receipt, $24.99 does not.

text: Approved claims are paid in the next monthly payroll run.
note: How payment works. Nothing in a claim can break it.

text: A meal with no client present may cost up to $60 per person.
A client meal costing over $75 per person must be approved by a director.
note: Over $75: exactly $75 does not need a director.

text: A client meal claim must list every attendee and the company they work for.
A business class flight is allowed only when the flight is longer than 6 hours, and only with pre-approval from a vice president.
note: Hours, not dollars. Longer than 6: exactly 6 is not enough.

text: Hotels are paid up to $220 a night, or up to $300 a night in New York, San Francisco and London.
note: Two limits per night. Either one is accepted as the high threshold.

text: Meals while travelling overnight are paid at the current per-diem rate published by Finance, instead of being claimed one by one.
note: The rate is not in the policy: it must be a parameter with no value, never a number from memory.

text: Any claim over $500 must be approved by a director.
note: Over $500: exactly $500 does not need a director.

text: No one may approve their own claim.
Managers are encouraged to review claims promptly, so that people are paid on time.
note: Encouraged, not required, and no deadline is given.
